Captain James Cook, still holding the rank of lieutenant, sights the eastern coast of what is now Australia.
Marie Antoinette marries Louis XVI in a proxy wedding.

Sierra Leone becomes a republic, and Siaka Stevens the president.
Launch of Salyut 1, the first space station.

South Vietnamese forces withdraw from the town of Xuan Loc in the last major battle of the Vietnam War.

main.t: Army of the Republic of Vietnam

links.t: Decision on the Capital of Germany

events.text: Forces of the Republic of Texas led by Sam Houston defeated the Mexican troops of Antonio López de Santa Anna in the Battle of San Jacinto, the decisive and final battle of the Texas Revolution.
Texas Revolution: The Battle of San Jacinto: Republic of Texas forces under Sam Houston defeat troops under Mexican General Antonio López de Santa Anna.
Australian labour movement: Stonemasons and building workers on building sites around Melbourne march from the University of Melbourne to Parliament House to achieve an eight-hour day.
Norway formally adopts the Krag–Jørgensen bolt-action rifle as the main arm of its armed forces, a weapon that would remain in service for almost 50 years.

Spanish–American War: The United States Navy begins a blockade of Cuban ports. When the U.S. Congress issued a declaration of war on April 25, it declared that a state of war had existed from this date.

main.desc: 1898 conflict between Spain and the United States

events.text: Ypiranga incident: A German arms shipment to Mexico is intercepted by the U.S. Navy near Veracruz.

main.desc: 1914 detention of a German ship by US forces

events.text: World War I: German fighter ace Manfred von Richthofen, better known as "The Red Baron", is shot down and killed over Vaux-sur-Somme in France.
Al-Baqi cemetery, former site of the mausoleum of four Shi'a Imams, is leveled to the ground by Wahhabis.

main.desc: First Islamic cemetery of Medina, Saudi Arabia

events.text: The "Surgeon's Photograph", the most famous photo allegedly showing the Loch Ness Monster, is published in the Daily Mail (in 1994, it is revealed to be a hoax).
World War II: Soviet forces south of Berlin at Zossen attack the German High Command headquarters.
The U.S. Weather Bureau records that a tornado which struck Timber Lake, South Dakota was 4 miles (6.4 km), among the widest tornadoes on record.

main.desc: U.S. forecasting agency of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration

links.t: List of United States tornadoes in 1946

events.text: United Nations Security Council Resolution 47 relating to Kashmir conflict is adopted.

main.desc: 1948 resolution on resolving the Kashmir conflict

events.text: The Nainital wedding massacre occurs, killing 22 members of the Harijan caste.
Secretary's Day (now Administrative Professionals' Day) is first celebrated.

main.desc: Day to recognize secretaries and others

events.text: United Airlines Flight 736 collided with a U.S. Air Force fighter jet over southern Nevada, resulting in the deaths of all 49 people on board both aircraft.
United Air Lines Flight 736 collides with a United States Air Force fighter jet near Arden, Nevada in what is now Enterprise, Nevada.
Brasília, a planned city primarily designed by architect and urban planner Lúcio Costa, was officially inaugurated, replacing Rio de Janeiro as the capital of Brazil.
Brasília, Brazil's capital, is officially inaugurated. At 09:30, the Three Powers of the Republic are simultaneously transferred from the old capital, Rio de Janeiro.
The Century 21 Exposition, the first world's fair in the United States since World War II, opened in Seattle.

main.desc: World's fair held in Seattle, Washington

events.text: The Seattle World's Fair (Century 21 Exposition) opens. It is the first World's Fair in the United States since World War II.

main.desc: World's fair held in Seattle, Washington

events.text: The first election of the Universal House of Justice is held, marking its establishment as the supreme governing institution of the Baháʼí Faith.

main.desc: Elected institution governing the worldwide Baháʼí community

events.text: A Transit-5bn satellite fails to reach orbit after launch; as it re-enters the atmosphere, 2.1 pounds (0.95 kg) of radioactive plutonium in its SNAP RTG power source is widely dispersed.
The 1964–1965 New York World's Fair opens for its second and final season.

main.desc: World's fair held in New York City

events.text: Rastafari movement: Haile Selassie of Ethiopia visits Jamaica, an event now celebrated as Grounation Day.

main.desc: Abrahamic new religious movement originating in 1930s Jamaica

events.text: A violent tornado strikes multiple schools and destroys houses in Belvidere, Illinois, United States, causing over 450 casualties.
A few days before the general election in Greece, Colonel George Papadopoulos leads a coup d'état, establishing a military regime that lasts for seven years.

main.desc: Election in which all or most members of a given political body are chosen

events.text: A tornado outbreak in Illinois, United States, kills over 50 and injures over 1,000. Belvidere sustains over 500 casualties as a violent tornado strikes the high school. Another tornado near Chicago causes another 500 casualties, devastating Oak Lawn.

main.desc: Weather event in the United States

events.text: In response to a dispute over wheat production quotas, Leonard Casley declared his 75 km2 (29 sq mi) farm in Western Australia to be an independent country as the Hutt River Province.
Astronauts John Young and Charles Duke fly Apollo 16's Apollo Lunar Module to the Moon's surface, the fifth NASA Apollo Program crewed lunar landing.
South Vietnamese president Nguyễn Văn Thiệu resigned on hearing of the fall of Xuân Lộc, the last battle of the Vietnam War.
Vietnam War: President of South Vietnam Nguyễn Văn Thiệu flees Saigon, as Xuân Lộc, the last South Vietnamese outpost blocking a direct North Vietnamese assault on Saigon, falls.
Annie opens on Broadway.
Baseball: Rollie Fingers of the Milwaukee Brewers becomes the first pitcher to record 300 saves.
The compound of the militant group The Covenant, The Sword, and the Arm of the Lord surrenders to federal authorities in Arkansas after a two-day government siege.

main.t: The Covenant, the Sword, and the Arm of the Lord
main.desc: American far-right militant group active during the 1970s and 80s

events.text: The Tamil Tigers are blamed for a car bomb that detonates in the Sri Lankan capital city of Colombo, killing 106 people.

main.desc: Tamil militant organisation in Sri Lanka (1976–2009)

events.text: Tiananmen Square protests of 1989: In Beijing, around 100,000 students gather in Tiananmen Square to commemorate Chinese reform leader Hu Yaobang.
The Supreme Court in La Paz, Bolivia, sentences former dictator Luis García Meza to 30 years in jail without parole for murder, theft, fraud and violating the constitution.
Four people are killed and 75 are injured in a train accident in Jokela, Finland.

main.desc: Train accident in Tuusula, Finland, on 21 April 1996

events.text: Five suicide car bombers target police stations in and around Basra, killing 74 people and wounding 160.

main.desc: Bombing of police stations in Basra, Iraq

events.text: Ukraine and Russia signed the Kharkiv Pact, extending the Russian lease on naval facilities in Crimea.

The controversial Kharkiv Pact (Russian Ukrainian Naval Base for Gas Treaty) is signed in Kharkiv, Ukraine, by Ukrainian president Viktor Yanukovych and Russian president Dmitry Medvedev; it was unilaterally terminated by Russia on March 31, 2014.
Two trains are involved in a head-on collision near Sloterdijk, Amsterdam, in the Netherlands, killing one person and injuring 116 others.
The city of Flint, Michigan, U.S., changed its water source to the Flint River, which exposed residents to lead poisoning.a
Eight bombs explode at churches, hotels, and other locations in Sri Lanka on Easter Sunday, killing at least 269.
The Indonesian Navy submarine Nanggala imploded and sank in the Bali Sea, resulting in the deaths of all 53 people on board.

main.desc: Maritime service branch of the Indonesian National Armed Forces

events.text: Indonesian Navy submarine KRI Nanggala (402) sinks in the Bali Sea during a military drill, killing all 53 on board.

main.desc: Maritime service branch of the Indonesian National Armed Forces

events.text: Basil II is crowned co-Emperor of the Byzantine Empire.
Gregory VII was elected pope following the death of Alexander II.

main.desc: Head of the Catholic Church from 1073 to 1085

events.text: Election of Pope Gregory VII following the death of Pope Alexander II.

main.desc: Head of the Catholic Church from 1073 to 1085

events.text: A fleet commanded by Pedro Álvares Cabral (pictured) anchored off present-day Brazil; he later claimed the land for the Portuguese Empire.
Portuguese navigator Pedro Álvares Cabral lands in Brazil (discovery of Brazil).
Spanish conquistador Hernán Cortés establishes a settlement at Veracruz, Mexico.

main.desc: Spanish and Portuguese colonizers of the Age of Discovery

events.text: Treaty of Zaragoza divides the eastern hemisphere between Spain and Portugal along a line 297.5 leagues (1,250 kilometres (780 mi)) east of the Moluccas.

main.desc: 1529 peace treaty between Spain and Portugal

events.text: Anglo-Persian forces combined to capture the Portuguese garrison at Hormuz Island in the Persian Gulf.
The second day of the Battle of Eckmühl: The Austrian army is defeated by the First French Empire army led by Napoleon and driven over the Danube in Regensburg.

main.desc: 1809 battle of the War of the Fifth Coalition

events.text: Texas Revolution: A day after the Battle of San Jacinto, forces under Texas General Sam Houston identify Mexican General Antonio López de Santa Anna among the captives of the battle when some of his fellow soldiers mistakenly give away his identity.
U.S. Congress passed the Coinage Act, which authorized the minting of the two-cent piece (pictured), the first U.S. coin to bear the phrase "In God We Trust".

main.desc: 1864 U.S. federal legislation regulating one- and two-cent coins

events.text: The U.S. Congress passes the Coinage Act of 1864 that permitted the inscription In God We Trust be placed on all coins minted as United States currency.

main.desc: Bicameral legislature of the United States

events.text: The first National League baseball game is played at the Jefferson Street Grounds in Philadelphia.
The first meeting of the Colonial Defence Committee, a standing committee of the British Colonial Office, was held to discuss the defence of Barbados.
At noon, thousands rush to claim land in the Land Rush of 1889. Within hours the cities of Oklahoma City and Guthrie are formed with populations of at least 10,000.
Spanish–American War: President William McKinley calls for 125,000 volunteers to join the National Guard and fight in Cuba, while Congress more than doubles regular Army forces to 65,000.

main.desc: 1898 conflict between Spain and the United States

events.text: The 1906 Intercalated Games open in Athens.
World War I: The use of poison gas in World War I escalates when chlorine gas is released as a chemical weapon in the Second Battle of Ypres.

links.t: Chemical weapons in World War I

events.text: The short-lived Transcaucasian Democratic Federative Republic was established on territory formerly part of the Russian Empire.

main.desc: 1918 month-long state in the South Caucasus

events.text: The United Kingdom, Japan and the United States sign the London Naval Treaty regulating submarine warfare and limiting shipbuilding.
World War II:  The 1st Air Commando Group using Sikorsky R-4 helicopters stage the first use of helicopters in combat with combat search and rescue operations in the China Burma India Theater.
World War II: In Greenland, the Allied Sledge Patrol attack the German Bassgeiger weather station.
World War II: Operation Persecution is initiated: Allied forces land in the Hollandia (currently known as Jayapura) area of New Guinea.

main.desc: Battle of the Western New Guinea campaign of World War II

events.text: About 600 prisoners of the Jasenovac concentration camp in the Independent State of Croatia revolted, but only 80 managed to escape while the remainder were killed by the Ustaše regime.

main.desc: Concentration camp run by the Ustaše in occupied Yugoslavia during World War II

events.text: World War II: Prisoners at the Jasenovac concentration camp revolt. Five hundred twenty are killed and around eighty escape.

main.desc: Concentration camp run by the Ustaše in occupied Yugoslavia during World War II

events.text: World War II: Sachsenhausen concentration camp is liberated by soldiers of the Red Army and Polish First Army.

main.desc: Nazi concentration camp in Oranienburg, Germany

events.text: Civil War in Mandatory Palestine: The Jewish paramilitary group Haganah captured Haifa from the Arab Liberation Army.

main.desc: First phase of the 1947–1949 Palestine war

events.text: Arab–Israeli War: The port city of Haifa is captured by Jewish forces.

main.desc: Second and final stage of the 1948 Palestine war

events.text: Korean War: The Chinese People's Volunteer Army attacked positions occupied mainly by Australian and Canadian forces, starting the Battle of Kapyong.
Korean War: The Chinese People's Volunteer Army begin assaulting positions defended by the Royal Australian Regiment and the Princess Patricia's Canadian Light Infantry at the Battle of Kapyong.
Red Scare: Witnesses begin testifying and live television coverage of the Army–McCarthy hearings begins.

main.desc: Phenomenon of US political rhetoric after WWII

events.text: American Flyers Airline Flight 280/D crashes on approach to Ardmore Municipal Airport in Ardmore, Oklahoma, killing 83.
British yachtsman Sir Robin Knox-Johnston wins the Sunday Times Golden Globe Race and completes the first solo non-stop circumnavigation of the world.
The formation of the Communist Party of India (Marxist–Leninist) is announced at a mass rally in Calcutta.

main.desc: Far-left political party in India from 1969 to 1972

events.text: The first Earth Day is celebrated.
Chicano residents in San Diego, California occupy a site under the Coronado Bridge, leading to the creation of Chicano Park.
Pan Am Flight 812 crashes on approach to Ngurah Rai International Airport in Denpasar, Bali, Indonesia, killing all 107 people on board.
Optical fiber is first used to carry live telephone traffic.
A series of gas explosions rip through the streets in Guadalajara, Mexico, killing 206.

main.desc: Ignition of air and flammable gas

events.text: Stephen Lawrence, a black British teenager, was murdered while waiting for a bus in Eltham, London, leading to cultural changes of attitudes on racism and the police, and to the law and police practice.

main.desc: British people of sub-Saharan African descent

events.text: Eighteen-year-old Stephen Lawrence is murdered in a racially motivated attack while waiting for a bus in Well Hall, Eltham.
In a pre-dawn raid, U.S. federal agents seized six-year-old Elián González from his relatives' home in Miami and returned him to his Cuban father.

main.desc: Cuban boy in 2000 international custody dispute

events.text: Flammable cargo exploded at a railway station in Ryongchon, North Korea, killing at least 54 people and injuring more than a thousand others.
Japan's Prime Minister Junichiro Koizumi apologizes for Japan's war record.

main.desc: Prime Minister of Japan from 2001 to 2006

links.t: List of war apology statements issued by Japan

events.text: The Royal Canadian Mounted Police arrested two men who were plotting to commit terrorist attacks against Via Rail operations.
The Paris Agreement, an international treaty on climate change, opened for signature and was signed by 175 parties.

links.t: List of parties to the Paris Agreement

events.text: The Paris Agreement is signed, an agreement to help fight global warming.
A truck struck and killed four Victoria Police officers on the Eastern Freeway, Australia, the force's deadliest single incident.

Four police officers are killed after being struck by a truck on the Eastern Freeway in Melbourne while speaking to a speeding driver, marking the largest loss of police lives in Victoria Police history.
American climate activist Wynn Bruce set himself on fire outside the United States Supreme Court Building in an apparent protest against the climate crisis.

main.desc: 2022 suicide of climate activist in Washington, D.C., U.S.

events.text: At least 26 people are killed in a terrorist attack on a group of tourists in Pahalgam, Jammu and Kashmir. The Resistance Front (TRF), an offshoot of the Pakistan-based militant group Lashkar-e-Taiba claimed responsibility for the attack.

main.desc: Islamist terrorist attack in Indian-administered Kashmir

events.text: A temple is built on the Capitoline Hill dedicated to Venus Erycina to commemorate the Roman defeat at Lake Trasimene.
Maya king Uneh Chan of Calakmul attacks rival city-state Palenque in southern Mexico, defeating queen Yohl Ik'nal and sacking the city.
Dagobert III succeeds his father King Childebert III as King of the Franks.
The Vikings were defeated by the Irish at the Battle of Clontarf.
Battle of Clontarf: High King of Ireland Brian Boru defeats Viking invaders, but is killed in battle.

main.desc: 1014 battle between the Kingdom of Ireland and an Irish-Norse alliance

events.text: Edmund Ironside became King of England, reigning for only seven months before the country was conquered by Cnut the Great.
Edmund Ironside succeeds his father Æthelred the Unready as King of England.
St. George's Night Uprising commences in the Duchy of Estonia.
The first knights of the Order of the Garter, an order of chivalry founded by King Edward III of England, were appointed.

main.desc: Honorary title awarded for service to a state or church

events.text: The founding of the Order of the Garter by King Edward III is announced on St. George's Day.
Albanian commander Skanderbeg entered Krujë, breaking a 10-month siege by Ottoman forces.
Ottoman wars in Europe: Albanian leader Skanderbeg defeated an Ottoman army under Ballaban Badera to raise the siege of Krujë.

main.desc: Series of military conflicts between the Ottoman Empire and various European states

events.text: Portuguese explorer Pedro Alvarez Cabral reaches new coastline (Brazil).
The Munich Reinheitsgebot (regarding the ingredients of beer) takes effect in all of Bavaria.
Battle of Villalar: King Charles I of Spain defeats the Comuneros.

main.desc: 1521 battle during the Revolt of the Comuneros

events.text: The first public school in the United States, the Boston Latin School, is founded.
The Siege of Santo Domingo begins during the Anglo-Spanish War, and fails seven days later.
Treaty of Oliva is established between Sweden and Poland.

main.desc: 1660 peace treaty to end the Second Northern War

events.text: Charles II was crowned King of England, Scotland and Ireland at Westminster Abbey.

main.desc: King of England, Scotland, and Ireland from 1660 to 1685

events.text: King Charles II of England, Scotland and Ireland is crowned in Westminster Abbey.

main.desc: King of England, Scotland, and Ireland from 1660 to 1685

events.text: Succeeding Charles II, his late brother, James II was crowned King of England, becoming last Catholic to hold the title.

main.desc: King of England, Scotland, and Ireland from 1660 to 1685

events.text: Johann Sebastian Bach leads the first performance of his cantata Du Hirte Israel, höre, BWV 104, illustrating the topic of the Good Shepherd in pastoral music.
The Second Serbian Uprising: A second phase of the national revolution of the Serbs against the Ottoman Empire, erupts shortly after the annexation of the country to the Ottoman Empire.

main.desc: 1815–17 rebellion within Serbia following its re-annexation by the Ottoman Empire

events.text: Fire burns down the second main building and dome of the University of Notre Dame, which prompts the construction of the third, and current, Main Building with its golden dome.

main.desc: Catholic university in Notre Dame, Indiana, U.S.

events.text: Chilean Civil War: The armored frigate Blanco Encalada (pictured) was sunk at the Battle of Caldera Bay, the first ironclad warship lost to a self-propelled torpedo.

main.desc: Conflict between the Army (pro-President) and Navy (pro-Congress)

events.text: Chilean Civil War: The ironclad Blanco Encalada is sunk at Caldera Bay by torpedo boats.

main.desc: Conflict between the Army (pro-President) and Navy (pro-Congress)

events.text: In Portugal, a magnitude 6.0 earthquake strikes near Lisbon, killing at least 60 people and injuring 75.
First World War: The British Royal Navy launched unsuccessful raids on Ostend and Zeebrugge in German-occupied Belgium.
World War I: The British Royal Navy makes a raid in an attempt to neutralise the Belgian port of Bruges-Zeebrugge.
The Estonian Constituent Assembly is held in Estonia, which marks the birth of the Estonian Parliament, the Riigikogu.
The Grand National Assembly of Turkey, the country's unicameral legislature, first met in Ankara in the midst of the Turkish War of Independence.
The Grand National Assembly of Turkey (TBMM) is founded in Ankara. The assembly denounces the government of Sultan Mehmed VI and announces the preparation of a temporary constitution.
Cardiff City defeated Arsenal 1–0 in the FA Cup final (match programme pictured) in the only time the FA Cup has been won by a non-English team.

main.desc: Association football club in Cardiff, Wales

events.text: Cardiff City defeat Arsenal in the FA Cup Final, the only time it has been won by a team not based in England.

main.desc: Association football club in Cardiff, Wales

events.text: The Polish Constitution of 1935 is adopted.

main.desc: 2nd constitution of the Second Polish Republic, adopted in 1935

events.text: The Rhythm Club fire at a dance hall in Natchez, Mississippi, kills 198 people.

main.desc: 1940 dance hall fire in Mississippi that killed 209

events.text: World War II: The Greek government and King George II evacuate Athens before the invading Wehrmacht.
Second World War: In retaliation for the Royal Air Force's bombing of Lübeck, the Luftwaffe began a series of air raids across England, beginning with Exeter.

links.t: Bombing of Lübeck in World War II

events.text: World War II: Baedeker Blitz: German bombers hit Exeter, Bath and York in retaliation for the British raid on Lübeck.

main.desc: German air raids on British cities during World War II

events.text: World War II: The US Army's 90th Infantry Division liberated Flossenbürg concentration camp (pictured) in Germany, freeing 1,500 prisoners.

World War II: Adolf Hitler's designated successor, Hermann Göring, sends him a telegram asking permission to take leadership of Nazi Germany. Martin Bormann and Joseph Goebbels advise Göring that the telegram is treasonous.
Manuel Roxas is elected the last President of the Commonwealth of the Philippines.

main.desc: President of the Philippines from 1946 to 1948

events.text: Chinese Civil War: Establishment of the People's Liberation Army Navy.
American journalist William N. Oatis was arrested for espionage by the communist government of Czechoslovakia.
Cold War: American journalist William N. Oatis is arrested for espionage by the Communist government of Czechoslovakia.

main.desc: 1947–1991 geopolitical rivalry between US and USSR

events.text: Batting for the Milwaukee Braves against Vic Raschi of the St. Louis Cardinals, Hank Aaron hit the first of his 755 home runs in Major League Baseball.

main.desc: Baseball offensive act of facing the pitcher and attempting to hit the ball into play

events.text: During the Algiers putsch by French generals, President Charles de Gaulle announces he has assumed emergency powers, and calls on troops and civilians to support him.

main.desc: Attempted coup in French Algeria during the Algerian War

events.text: Aeroflot Flight 2723 crashes into the Caspian Sea off the Absheron Peninsula, killing 33 people.
Soviet space program: Soyuz 1 (Russian: Союз 1, Union 1), a crewed spaceflight carrying cosmonaut Colonel Vladimir Komarov, is launched into orbit.

main.desc: Space exploration program conducted by the Soviet Union from 1951 to 1991

events.text: Vietnam War: Student protesters at Columbia University in New York City take over administration buildings and shut down the university.
The Rolling Stones released Sticky Fingers, the first album on their own label, Rolling Stones Records.
Bangladesh Liberation War: The Pakistan Army and Razakars massacre approximately 3,000 Hindu emigrants in the Jathibhanga area of East Pakistan (now Bangladesh).
The American band the Ramones released their debut album, which became highly influential on the emerging punk rock movement.
Blair Peach, a New Zealand teacher, was fatally injured while taking part in an Anti-Nazi League demonstration against a National Front election meeting in Southall, London.

main.desc: 1979 police killing of a protestor in London

events.text: SAETA Flight 011 crashes in Pastaza Province, Ecuador, killing all 57 people on board. The wreckage was not discovered until 1984.
Blair Peach, a British activist, is fatally injured after being knocked unconscious during an Anti-Nazi League demonstration against a National Front election meeting in Southall, London.

main.desc: 1979 police killing of a protestor in London

events.text: The ZX Spectrum (pictured), Britain's best-selling microcomputer, was released.
Coca-Cola changes its formula and releases New Coke. The response is overwhelmingly negative, and the original formula is back on the market in less than three months.
Namibia becomes the 160th member of the United Nations and the 50th member of the Commonwealth of Nations.

links.t: Member states of the United Nations
Member states of the Commonwealth of Nations

events.text: Eritreans vote overwhelmingly for independence from Ethiopia in a United Nations-monitored referendum.

main.desc: Country in the Horn of Africa

events.text: Sri Lankan politician Lalith Athulathmudali is assassinated while addressing a gathering, approximately four weeks ahead of the Provincial Council elections for the Western Province.
NATO bombs the headquarters of Radio Television of Serbia, as part of their aerial campaign against the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

links.t: NATO bombing of the Radio Television of Serbia headquarters

events.text: The first YouTube video, titled "Me at the zoo", is published by co-founder Jawed Karim.
The gamma-ray burst GRB 090423 was detected coming from the most distant astronomical object of any kind known at the time.

main.desc: Flash of gamma rays from a distant galaxy

links.t: List of the most distant astronomical objects

events.text: Arizona governor Jan Brewer signed into law the controversial anti–illegal immigration bill SB 1070, much of which was later struck down by the U.S. Supreme Court.
At least 111 people are killed and 233 injured as violence breaks out in Hawija, Iraq.

main.desc: Violence in northern Iraq during the post-U.S. insurgency

events.text: A man intentionally struck pedestrians with a van on Yonge Street in Toronto, Canada, leading to 11 deaths.
A vehicle-ramming attack kills 11 people and injures 15 in Toronto. A 25-year-old suspect, Alek Minassian, is arrested.
The April 2019 Hpakant jade mine collapse in Myanmar kills four miners and two rescuers, with at least 50 others missing and presumed dead.

main.desc: Fatal incident in Kachin State, Myanmar

events.text: The 2024 Lumut mid-air collision in Malaysia kills 10 people while rehearsing for the 90th anniversary of the Royal Malaysian Navy.

main.desc: Crash of two Royal Malaysian Navy helicopters

events.text: Thutmose III ascends to the throne of Egypt, although power effectively shifts to Hatshepsut (according to the Low Chronology of the 18th dynasty).

main.desc: Pharaoh of Egypt from 1479 to 1425 BC

events.text: Traditional reckoning of the Fall of Troy marking the end of the legendary Trojan War, given by chief librarian of the Library of Alexandria Eratosthenes, among others.

main.desc: Ancient city in northwest Asia Minor

events.text: Consecration of Pope Nicholas I following the death of Pope Benedict III earlier that month.

main.desc: Head of the Catholic Church from 858 to 867

events.text: Abbasid Caliph Al-Qahir is deposed and blinded. His nephew al-Radi succeeds him as caliph.
Battle of Mühlberg. Duke of Alba, commanding Spanish-Imperial forces of Charles I of Spain, defeats the troops of Schmalkaldic League.

links.t: Fernando Álvarez de Toledo, 3rd Duke of Alba

events.text: Mary, Queen of Scots, marries the Dauphin of France, François, at Notre-Dame de Paris.

links.t: Wedding of Mary, Queen of Scots, and Francis, Dauphin of France

events.text: John Campbell released the first issue of The Boston News-Letter, the first continuously published newspaper in British North America.
The first regular newspaper in British Colonial America, The Boston News-Letter, is published.

main.desc: British colonies forming the United States

events.text: French revolutionary Jean-Paul Marat is acquitted by the Revolutionary Tribunal of charges brought by the Girondin in Paris.

A fire broke out in Surat, India, which went on to destroy about 75% of the city.
The great fire in Surat, India causes more than 500 deaths and destruction of more than 9,000 houses.
German composer Max Bruch (pictured) conducted the premiere of his first violin concerto.
Russo-Turkish War: The Russian Empire declares war on the Ottoman Empire.

main.desc: Eleventh and penultimate conflict of the Russo-Turkish wars

events.text: American sharpshooter Annie Oakley is hired by Nate Salsbury to be a part of Buffalo Bill's Wild West.

main.desc: One who is highly proficient with firearms

main.desc: 19th-century Canadian-American seaman; first to circumnavigate the world solo

main.desc: Measures to increase the influence of Russian culture and language

events.text: The Woolworth Building in New York City officially opened; at the time, it was the tallest building in the world, with a height of 792 ft (241 m).

main.desc: 1914 confirmation of the atom's quantum nature

main.desc: Radiotelegraphic communications network within the British Empire in the 20th century

events.text: Thorvald Stauning becomes premier of Denmark (first term).
The Treaty of Berlin is signed. Germany and the Soviet Union each pledge neutrality in the event of an attack on the other by a third party for the next five years.

The State Duma of the Russian Empire meets for the first time.

main.desc: Legislative assembly in the Russian Empire (1906-1917)

events.text: Sultan of Ottoman Empire Abdul Hamid II is overthrown, and is succeeded by his brother, Mehmed V.

main.desc: Noble title with several historical meanings

events.text: The Second Canton Uprising took place but was suppressed in Guangzhou, China.
The Second Canton Uprising takes place in Guangzhou, Qing China, but is suppressed.
Carabineros de Chile (Chilean national police force and gendarmerie) are created.
The trilogy The Adventure Girls (second book pictured), by the children's author Clair Blank, was copyrighted by A. L. Burt.
The United Auto Workers (UAW) gains autonomy from the American Federation of Labor.
World War II: German troops enter Athens.
World War II: The photograph Raising the Flag on the Three-Country Cairn (pictured) was taken after German troops withdrew to Norway at the end of the Lapland War.

links.t: Raising the Flag on the Three-Country Cairn

events.text: World War II: The last German formations withdraw from Finland to Norway. The Lapland War and thus, World War II in Finland, comes to an end and the Raising the Flag on the Three-Country Cairn photograph is taken.

links.t: Raising the Flag on the Three-Country Cairn

events.text: World War II: Benito Mussolini is arrested by Italian partisans in Dongo, while attempting escape disguised as a German soldier.
In response to the treatment of Lorenzo Gamboa under the White Australia policy, the Philippine House of Representatives passed a bill banning Australians from the country.

links.t: House of Representatives of the Philippines

events.text: Operation Moolah offers $50,000 to any pilot who defects with a fully mission-capable Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-15 to South Korea. The first pilot was to receive $100,000.

main.desc: US Air Force effort to obtain a Soviet MiG-15

events.text: Prime Minister Milton Margai led the Sierra Leone Colony and Protectorate to independence from the United Kingdom.

main.desc: Sierra Leone head of government from 1954 to 1964

events.text: Indonesia–Malaysia confrontation: British forces repelled a surprise Indonesian attack on a base at Plaman Mapu in Sarawak.
The Expo 67 world's fair opened in Montreal, with 62 nations participating and more than 50 million visitors ultimately attending.

main.desc: World's fair held in Montreal, Quebec

events.text: Expo 67 officially opens in Montreal, Quebec, Canada with a large opening ceremony broadcast around the world. It opens to the public the next day.

main.desc: World's fair held in Montreal, Quebec

events.text: One hundred nine people are killed in a plane crash near Pulkovo Airport.

main.desc: 1974 aviation accident in the Soviet Union

events.text: Thirty-seven people are killed when American Airlines Flight 625 crashes at Cyril E. King Airport in Saint Thomas, U.S. Virgin Islands.

main.desc: 1976 aviation accident in the United States Virgin Islands

events.text: John Ehrlichman, a former aide to U.S. President Richard Nixon, is released from the Federal Correctional Institution, Safford, Arizona, after serving 18 months for Watergate-related crimes.

main.desc: American lawyer, Watergate co-conspirator, and writer (1925–1999)

events.text: The Saur Revolution begins in Afghanistan, ending the following morning with the murder of Afghan President Mohammed Daoud Khan and the establishment of the Democratic Republic of Afghanistan.

Willow Island disaster: In the deadliest construction accident in United States history, 51 construction workers are killed when a cooling tower under construction collapses at the Pleasants Power Station in Willow Island, West Virginia.
The black-ball final, one of the most famous snooker matches in history, began between Steve Davis and Dennis Taylor.
The city of Pripyat and surrounding areas are evacuated due to the Chernobyl disaster.

main.desc: Abandoned city in Kyiv Oblast, Ukraine

events.text: The U.S. Department of Justice bars Austrian President Kurt Waldheim (and his wife, Elisabeth, who had also been a Nazi) from entering the US, charging that he had aided in the deportations and executions of thousands of Jews and others as a German Army officer during World War II.
The April 27 demonstrations, student-led protests responding to the April 26 Editorial, during the Tiananmen Square protests of 1989.

main.desc: 1989 nationwide Chinese student protests in response to the April 26 Editorial

events.text: The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, comprising Serbia and Montenegro, is proclaimed.
Betty Boothroyd becomes the first woman to be elected Speaker of the British House of Commons in its 700-year history.

links.t: 1992 Speaker of the British House of Commons election
Speaker of the House of Commons (United Kingdom)
House of Commons of the United Kingdom

events.text: The Russian Federation and 12 other former Soviet republics become members of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank.

main.desc: Country in Eastern Europe and North Asia

events.text: Thirty people died, including players and staff of the Zambia football team and the crew, in a plane crash en route to play a World Cup qualifying match against Senegal.

links.t: 1993 Zambia national football team plane crash

events.text: Most of the Zambia national football team lose their lives in a plane crash off Libreville, Gabon en route to Dakar, Senegal to play a 1994 FIFA World Cup qualifying match against Senegal.

links.t: 1993 Zambia national football team plane crash

events.text: South African general election: The first democratic general election in South Africa, in which black citizens could vote. The Interim Constitution comes into force.This marked the end of Apartheid.

main.desc: First South African election held under nonracial, universal suffrage

events.text: American spree killer Andrew Cunanan murdered Jeffrey Trail, a former friend and a Gulf War veteran, who became the first victim of Cunanan's killing spree.
The Airbus A380, the world's largest passenger airliner, made its maiden flight from Toulouse, France.
Airbus A380 aircraft has its maiden test flight.
Construction begins on the Freedom Tower (later renamed One World Trade Center) in New York City.
Estonian authorities remove the Bronze Soldier, a Soviet Red Army war memorial in Tallinn, amid political controversy with Russia.
Israeli archaeologists discover the tomb of Herod the Great south of Jerusalem.
During the most active day of the 2011 Super Outbreak 218 tornadoes killed 317 people across 16 U.S. states.

main.desc: Largest tornado outbreak in recorded history

events.text: The 2011 Super Outbreak devastates parts of the Southeastern United States, especially the states of Alabama, Mississippi, Georgia, and Tennessee. Two hundred five tornadoes touched down on April 27 alone, killing more than 300 and injuring hundreds more.

main.desc: Largest tornado outbreak in recorded history

events.text: Unknown perpetrators carried out a series of four bombings in Dnipropetrovsk, Ukraine.
At least four explosions hit the Ukrainian city of Dnipropetrovsk with at least 27 people injured.
The Panmunjom Declaration is signed between North and South Korea, officially declaring their intentions to end the Korean conflict.

main.desc: 2018 peace and denuclearisation agreement between North and South Korea

events.text: A train crash  kills at least 15 people and injures 84 others near Jakarta, Indonesia.

main.desc: Train collision in West Java, Indonesia

events.text: The ancient Iranian Parthian Empire fell to the Sasanids after its forces were defeated at the Battle of Hormozdgan.
The Battle of Hormozdgan is fought. Ardashir I defeats and kills Artabanus V, effectively ending the Parthian Empire.

main.desc: Battle between Parthian and Sasanian dynasties in 224

events.text: Emperor Constantius II enters Rome for the first time to celebrate his victory over Magnus Magnentius.
Assassination of Conrad of Montferrat (Conrad I), King of Jerusalem, in Tyre, two days after his title to the throne is confirmed by election. The killing is carried out by Hashshashin.

main.desc: Italian nobleman and crusader, King of Jerusalem from 1190 to 1192

events.text: The Japanese monk Nichiren declared the mantra Namu Myōhō Renge Kyō, now a central part of Nichiren Buddhism.

main.desc: Japanese Buddhist monk and philosopher and True Buddha (1222–1282)

events.text: Nichiren, a Japanese Buddhist monk, propounds Namu Myōhō Renge Kyō for the first time and declares it to be the essence of Buddhism, in effect founding Nichiren Buddhism.

main.desc: Japanese Buddhist monk and philosopher and True Buddha (1222–1282)

events.text: Temür, grandson of Kublai, is elected Khagan of the Mongols with the reigning title Oljeitu.

main.desc: Emperor of Yuan China from 1294 to 1307

events.text: The Battle of Cerignola is fought. It is noted as one of the first European battles in history won by small arms fire using gunpowder.

main.desc: 1503 battle in the Third Italian War

events.text: The University of Santo Tomas (seminary building pictured) in Manila, one of the oldest existing universities in Asia and one of the world's largest Catholic universities by enrollment, was founded.

main.desc: Private university in Metro Manila, Philippines

events.text: Establishment of the Pontifical and Royal University of Santo Tomas, the Catholic University of the Philippines and the largest Catholic university in the world.

main.desc: Private university in Metro Manila, Philippines

events.text: A combined Spanish and Portuguese fleet of 52 ships commences the recapture of Bahia from the Dutch during the Dutch–Portuguese War.
Pope Clement XII issues the first papal condemnation of Freemasonry and formally prohibits Catholics from becoming Freemasons.

main.desc: Head of the Catholic Church from 1730 to 1740

events.text: The Marathas defeat the Afghans in the Battle of Attock and capture the city.
Second Anglo-Mysore War: British troops surrendered the fortress of Bednore in southwestern India to French and Mysorean forces; many of the prisoners were later murdered.

main.desc: War in south India from 1780 to 1784

events.text: Maryland becomes the seventh state to ratify the United States Constitution.
Fletcher Christian, the acting lieutenant on board the Royal Navy ship Bounty, led a mutiny against the commander William Bligh in the South Pacific.

The Mutiny on the Bounty occurs, with  the ship's captain, Lieutenant William Bligh and 18 sailors, set adrift, and the rebel crew setting sail for Tahiti.  Eventually the majority of rebels sail for Pitcairn Island.

main.desc: 1789 mutiny aboard the British Royal Navy ship HMS Bounty

events.text: France invades the Austrian Netherlands (present day Belgium and Luxembourg), beginning the French Revolutionary Wars.
Sardinians, headed by Giovanni Maria Angioy, start a revolution against the Savoy domination, expelling Viceroy Balbiano and his officials from Cagliari, the capital and largest city of the island.
The Armistice of Cherasco is signed by Napoleon Bonaparte and Vittorio Amedeo III, King of Sardinia, expanding French territory along the Mediterranean coast.
Indian Rebellion of 1857: The Bawani Imli massacre saw 52 Indian freedom fighters hanged by British forces.
The Bawani Imli massacre, where 52 Indian freedom fighters are hanged to death on a tamarind tree by British colonial forces.
The sailing clipper ship Pomona is wrecked on the coast of Ireland with the loss of 424 of the 448 passengers and crew aboard.
Chinese and Irish laborers for the Central Pacific Railroad working on the first transcontinental railroad lay ten miles of track in one day, a feat which has never been matched.

main.desc: U.S. company that built western leg of the first transcontinental railroad

events.text: Billy the Kid escapes from the Lincoln County jail in Mesilla, New Mexico.
A week after being arrested by the Prussian Secret Police, French police inspector Guillaume Schnaebelé (pictured) was released on the order of William I, German Emperor, defusing a possible war.
A week after being arrested by the Prussian Secret Police, French police inspector Guillaume Schnaebelé is released on order of Wilhelm I, German Emperor, defusing a possible war.
Frenchman Louis Paulhan landed his biplane at Manchester, having departed from London the previous day, to win the world's first long-distance air race.
Frenchman Louis Paulhan wins the 1910 London to Manchester air race, the first long-distance aeroplane race in the United Kingdom.
The Azerbaijan Soviet Socialist Republic is founded.
The FA Cup final (crowd and police pictured) between Bolton Wanderers and West Ham United was held on the opening day of the Empire Stadium in London.
Wembley Stadium is opened, named initially as the Empire Stadium.

main.desc: Former stadium in Wembley Park, London

events.text: The Independence Producers host the first night game in the history of Organized Baseball in Independence, Kansas.
South African medical researcher Max Theiler develops the yellow fever vaccine at the Rockefeller Foundation in New York City.
World War II: Presaging a campaign of genocide against the Serbs of Croatia, around 190 people were massacred by members of the Ustaše movement in Gudovac.

links.t: Genocide of Serbs in the Independent State of Croatia

events.text: The Ustaše massacre nearly 200 Serbs in the village of Gudovac, the first massacre of their genocidal campaign against Serbs of the Independent State of Croatia.

links.t: Genocide of Serbs in the Independent State of Croatia

events.text: World War II: Nine German E-boats attack US and UK units during Exercise Tiger, the rehearsal for the Normandy landings, killing 946.
World War II: Benito Mussolini, the deposed fascist dictator of Italy, was executed by partisans in Giulino.
Benito Mussolini and his mistress Clara Petacci are shot dead by Walter Audisio, a member of the Italian resistance movement.
The Holocaust: Nazi Germany carries out its final use of gas chambers to execute 33 Upper Austrian socialist and communist leaders in Mauthausen concentration camp.

main.desc: Genocide of European Jews by Nazi Germany

events.text: Thor Heyerdahl and five crew mates set out from Peru on the Kon-Tiki to demonstrate that Peruvian natives could have settled Polynesia.
Igor Stravinsky conducts the premiere of his American ballet, Orpheus at the New York City Center.

The Hukbalahap are accused of assassinating former First Lady of the Philippines Aurora Quezon, while she is en route to dedicate a hospital in memory of her late husband; her daughter and ten others are also killed.

links.t: First ladies and gentlemen of the Philippines

events.text: Japan and the Republic of China signed the Treaty of Taipei, officially ending the Second Sino-Japanese War seven years after fighting ended due to World War II.

main.desc: 1952 peace treaty between Japan and the Republic of China

events.text: Dwight D. Eisenhower resigns as Supreme Allied Commander of NATO in order to campaign in the 1952 United States presidential election.

main.desc: World War II general, U.S. president from 1953 to 1961

events.text: The Treaty of San Francisco comes into effect, restoring Japanese sovereignty and ending its state of war with most of the Allies of World War II.
The Sino-Japanese Peace Treaty (Treaty of Taipei) is signed in Taipei, Taiwan between Japan and the Republic of China to officially end the Second Sino-Japanese War.

main.desc: 1952 peace treaty between Japan and the Republic of China

events.text: The Sibley Commission issued their final report, urging the government of the U.S. state of Georgia to abandon its strategy of massive resistance and legalize some instances of school integration.

main.desc: 1960 committee to investigate desegregation in Georgia

links.t: School integration in the United States

events.text: United States occupation of the Dominican Republic: American troops land in the Dominican Republic to "forestall establishment of a Communist dictatorship" and to evacuate US Army troops.

main.desc: 1965 civil war in the Dominican Republic

events.text: Vietnam War: Boxer Muhammad Ali refuses his induction into the United States Army and is subsequently stripped of his championship and license.
Charles de Gaulle resigns as President of France.
Vietnam War: US President Richard Nixon formally authorizes American combat troops to take part in the Cambodian campaign.
Scottish trade unionist Jimmy Reid condemned the capitalist "rat race" in his inaugural address as Rector of the University of Glasgow.

main.desc: Scottish trade union activist, orator, politician and journalist

links.t: Rector of the University of Glasgow

events.text: The album The Dark Side of the Moon by the British progressive rock band Pink Floyd entered the Billboard Top LPs & Tape chart, on which it spent a record 942 weeks.

main.t: The Dark Side of the Moon

events.text: The Dark Side of the Moon by Pink Floyd, recorded in Abbey Road Studios goes to number one on the US Billboard chart, beginning a record-breaking 741-week chart run.

main.t: The Dark Side of the Moon

events.text: General Cao Văn Viên, chief of the South Vietnamese military, departs for the US as the North Vietnamese Army closes in on victory.

links.t: Army of the Republic of Vietnam

events.text: The Red Army Faction trial ends, with Andreas Baader, Gudrun Ensslin and Jan-Carl Raspe found guilty of four counts of murder and more than 30 counts of attempted murder.
The President of Afghanistan, Mohammad Daoud Khan, is overthrown and assassinated in a coup led by pro-communist rebels.

main.desc: Former head of state and government

events.text: The West German news magazine Stern published excerpts from the purported diaries of Adolf Hitler, later revealed to be forgeries.
The West German news magazine Stern begins publishing excerpts from the purported diaries of Adolf Hitler, later revealed to be forgeries.
High levels of radiation resulting from the Chernobyl disaster are detected at Forsmark Nuclear Power Plant in Sweden, leading Soviet authorities to publicly announce the accident.

main.desc: 1986 nuclear accident in the Soviet Union

events.text: Aloha Airlines Flight 243 experienced explosive decompression while airborne between Hilo and Honolulu, Hawaii, with one fatality as a flight attendant was ejected from the aircraft.

main.desc: 1988 aviation accident over the Pacific Ocean

events.text: Near Maui, Hawaii, flight attendant Clarabelle "C.B." Lansing is blown out of Aloha Airlines Flight 243, a Boeing 737, and falls to her death when part of the plane's fuselage rips open in mid-flight.
Space Shuttle Discovery launches on STS-39, the first unclassified shuttle mission for the United States Department of Defense.
Former Central Intelligence Agency counterintelligence officer and analyst Aldrich Ames pleads guilty to giving US secrets to the Soviet Union and later Russia.

main.desc: U.S. intelligence and covert action agency

events.text: A spree shooter carried out the Port Arthur massacre, killing 35 people and injuring 23, in Tasmania, prompting stricter gun laws in Australia.

main.desc: Person killing in multiple locations in a short time

events.text: Whitewater controversy: President Bill Clinton gives a 41⁄2 hour videotaped testimony for the defense.
Port Arthur massacre, Tasmania: A gunman, Martin Bryant, opens fire at the Broad Arrow Cafe in Port Arthur, Tasmania, killing 35 people and wounding 23 others.
A 14-year-old former student in Taber, Alberta, opened fire at his high school, killing one student and wounding another in Canada's first fatal school shooting in more than two decades.

links.t: 1999 W. R. Myers High School shooting

events.text: CBS News releases evidence of the Abu Ghraib torture and prisoner abuse. The photographs show rape and abuse from the American troops over Iraqi detainees.

main.desc: News division of the American television and radio service CBS

links.t: Abu Ghraib torture and prisoner abuse

events.text: The 1,388-foot-tall (423.2 m) Trump International Hotel and Tower in Chicago, with the world's highest residence above ground level at the time, held its grand opening.

main.desc: Skyscraper in Chicago, Illinois, United States

events.text: An earthquake in the Central Apennines hits Rome and Spoleto, damaging the basilica of San Paolo Fuori le Mura.

links.t: Basilica of Saint Paul Outside the Walls

events.text: Battle of Levounion: The Pechenegs are defeated by Byzantine Emperor Alexios I Komnenos.
The Grand Duchy of Lithuania decisively won the Battle of the Vikhra River, forcibly making the Principality of Smolensk a vassal state.
Joan of Arc arrives to relieve the Siege of Orléans.
Gran Canaria, the main island of the Canary Islands, is conquered by the Kingdom of Castile.

main.desc: Spanish island in the North Atlantic

events.text: The Crown's decision to expel the Jews is announced in Zaragoza, Aragon, to the kingdom's procurators.

main.desc: Ethnic cleansing of Jews from Spain

events.text: Swedish War of Liberation: Swedish troops defeat a Danish force in the Battle of Västerås.

main.desc: 1521–1523 Swedish rebellion against King Christian II

events.text: Emilio Altieri is elected pope after a four-month conclave and takes the name Clement X.

main.desc: Election of Catholic Pope Clement X

events.text: Seven Years' War: France began an unsuccessful attempt to retake Quebec City, which had been captured by Britain.

links.t: Battle of the Plains of Abraham

events.text: French forces commence the siege of Quebec which is held by the British.

main.desc: Part of the Seven Years War

events.text: On his first voyage, British explorer James Cook and the crew of HMS Endeavour (pictured) landed at Botany Bay, making the first recorded European landfall on the eastern coast of Australia.

main.desc: Combined Royal Navy and Royal Society expedition to the south Pacific

events.text: James Cook arrives in Australia at Botany Bay, which he names.
American Revolutionary War: British and French ships clash in the Battle of Fort Royal off the coast of Martinique.
In Parramatta, Australia, Scottish astronomer James Dunlop discovered Centaurus A (pictured), which was later recognised as one of the nearest radio galaxies to Earth.

main.desc: City in New South Wales, Australia

events.text: The galaxy Centaurus A or NGC 5128 is discovered by James Dunlop.

main.desc: Radio galaxy in the constellation Centaurus

events.text: Maryland in the American Civil War: Maryland's House of Delegates votes not to secede from the Union.

main.t: Maryland in the American Civil War

events.text: American Civil War: The Capture of New Orleans by Union forces under David Farragut.
American Civil War: The Siege of Corinth begins as Union forces under General Henry Halleck move to engage Confederate forces led by General P. G. T. Beauregard.

main.desc: 1862 battle of the American Civil War

events.text: Confederate forts at Grand Gulf survived a bombardment by Union gunboats, preventing Ulysses S. Grant's troops from crossing the Mississippi River at that point.
Theta Xi fraternity is founded at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute, the only fraternity to be founded during the American Civil War.
A rockslide buried part of the Canadian mining town of Frank under 110 million tonnes of rock, killing around 70 people.

main.desc: Rockslide, buried part of Frank, Canada (1903)

events.text: A landslide kills 70 people in Frank, in the District of Alberta, Canada.

main.desc: Rockslide, buried part of Frank, Canada (1903)

events.text: Parliament passed the People's Budget, the first budget in British history with the express intent of redistributing wealth.
The Parliament of the United Kingdom passes the People's Budget, the first budget in British history with the expressed intent of redistributing wealth among the British public.
Tsinghua University, one of mainland China's leading universities, is founded.
World War I: The UK's 6th Indian Division surrenders to Ottoman Forces at the Siege of Kut in one of the largest surrenders of British forces up to that point.
Easter Rising: After six days of fighting, Irish rebel leaders surrender to British forces in Dublin, bringing the Easter Rising to an end.
Sixteen-year-old Lilian Salkeld became the first woman to walk from London to Brighton.

main.desc: Long-distance walking race held on public roads in England

events.text: After suffering train derailments, defections, and outbreaks of dysentery and typhoid fever which killed two members, the Brazilian football club Santa Cruz returned from their Suicidal Tour (team pictured).
Second World War: British agent Nancy Wake parachuted into Auvergne, France, becoming a liaison between the Special Operations Executive and the local Maquis group.
World War II: The U.S. Army liberated Dachau, the first Nazi concentration camp, and killed German prisoners of war.
World War II: The Surrender of Caserta is signed by the commander of German forces in Italy.
World War II:  Allied airdrops of food begin over German-occupied regions of the Netherlands.

main.desc: 1945 humanitarian food drops over the German-occupied Netherlands by the Allies

events.text: World War II: Adolf Hitler marries his longtime partner Eva Braun in a Berlin bunker and designates Admiral Karl Dönitz as his successor.
Dachau concentration camp is liberated by United States troops.
The International Military Tribunal for the Far East convenes and indicts former Prime Minister of Japan Hideki Tojo and 28 former Japanese leaders for war crimes.

main.t: International Military Tribunal for the Far East
main.desc: Post–World War II war crimes trials

events.text: Pan Am Flight 202 crashes into the Amazon basin near Carolina, Maranhão, Brazil, killing 50 people.
The first U.S. experimental 3D television broadcast shows an episode of Space Patrol on Los Angeles ABC affiliate KECA-TV.

main.desc: Television that conveys depth perception to the viewer

events.text: After refusing induction into the United States Army the previous day, Muhammad Ali is stripped of his boxing title.
The controversial Broadway musical Hair, a product of the counterculture of the 1960s, opened, with its songs becoming anthems of the anti-Vietnam War movement.

main.desc: Type of theatre in New York City

links.t: Opposition to United States involvement in the Vietnam War

events.text: Vietnam War: South Vietnamese forces began the Cambodian campaign, aiming to attack North Vietnamese jungle bases.
Vietnam War: United States and South Vietnamese forces invade Cambodia to interdict the Ho Chi Minh Trail in an attempt to cut off supplies to the Viet Cong and the North Vietnamese Army.
Watergate scandal: United States President Richard Nixon announces the release of edited transcripts of White House tape recordings relating to the scandal.
Vietnam War: North Vietnam concluded its East Sea Campaign by capturing all of the Spratly Islands held by South Vietnam.

Vietnam War: Operation Frequent Wind: The U.S. begins to evacuate U.S. citizens from Saigon before an expected North Vietnamese takeover. U.S. involvement in the war comes to an end. This happens after the Bombing of Tan Son Nhut Air Base.

links.t: Bombing of Tan Son Nhut Air Base

events.text: Vietnam War: The North Vietnamese Army completes its capture of all parts of South Vietnam-held Trường Sa Islands.
Space Shuttle Challenger is launched on STS-51-B.
A fire at the Central library of the Los Angeles Public Library damages or destroys 400,000 books and other items.

main.desc: Public library system in Los Angeles, California

events.text: The United States Navy aircraft carrier USS Enterprise becomes the first nuclear-powered aircraft carrier to transit the Suez Canal, navigating from the Red Sea to the Mediterranean Sea to relieve the USS Coral Sea.

main.desc: Warship that serves as a seagoing airbase

events.text: An assembly of Sikhs, known as a Sarbat Khalsa, officially declare independence for a state of Khalistan.
A powerful tropical cyclone struck Chittagong, Bangladesh, killing at least 138,000 people and leaving up to 10 million homeless across the region.
A cyclone strikes the Chittagong district of southeastern Bangladesh with winds of around 155 miles per hour (249 km/h), killing at least 138,000 people and leaving as many as ten million homeless.
The 7.0 Mw Racha earthquake affects Georgia with a maximum MSK intensity of IX (Destructive), killing 270 people.
The acquittal of policemen who had beaten African-American motorist Rodney King sparked six days of civil unrest in Los Angeles (damage pictured), during which 63 people were killed.

main.desc: Black American victim of police brutality (1965–2012)

events.text: Riots in Los Angeles begin, following the acquittal of police officers charged with excessive force in the beating of Rodney King. Over the next three days 63 people are killed and hundreds of buildings are destroyed.

main.desc: Riots and protests following the beating of Rodney King

events.text: Before a crowd of about 165,000 at the Rungrado 1st of May Stadium, Ric Flair and Antonio Inoki competed in the main event of Collision in Korea, the highest attended professional wrestling event of all time.

links.t: List of professional wrestling attendance records

events.text: The Chemical Weapons Convention entered into force, outlawing the production, stockpiling and use of chemical weapons in the 87 countries that had ratified the convention.

main.desc: Multilateral treaty prohibiting the production, stockpiling, and use of chemical weapons

links.t: List of parties to the Chemical Weapons Convention

events.text: The Chemical Weapons Convention of 1993 enters into force, outlawing the production, stockpiling and use of chemical weapons by its signatories.

main.desc: Multilateral treaty prohibiting the production, stockpiling, and use of chemical weapons

events.text: The final Oldsmobile is built in Lansing, Michigan, ending 107 years of vehicle production.

main.desc: Defunct entry-level luxury division of General Motors

events.text: Cyclone Mala made landfall near Thandwe, Myanmar, causing 37 deaths.
Watched by a worldwide television audience of tens of millions, Prince William and Catherine Middleton were married at Westminster Abbey in London.

main.desc: Heir apparent to the British throne (born 1982)

links.t: Wedding of Prince William and Catherine Middleton

events.text: The wedding of Prince William and Catherine Middleton takes place at Westminster Abbey in London.

main.t: Wedding of Prince William and Catherine Middleton

events.text: A powerful explosion occurs in an office building in Prague, believed to have been caused by natural gas, and injures 43 people.

main.desc: Blast caused by a natural gas leak

events.text: National Airlines Flight 102, a Boeing 747-400 freighter aircraft, crashes during takeoff from Bagram Airfield in Parwan Province, Afghanistan, killing all seven people on board.
The ringleaders of the Bali Nine were executed in Indonesia for attempting to smuggle 8.3 kg (18 lb) of heroin to Australia in 2005.

main.desc: Drug smugglers convicted in Indonesia in 2005

events.text: A baseball game between the Baltimore Orioles and the Chicago White Sox sets the all-time low attendance mark for Major League Baseball. Zero fans were in attendance for the game, as the stadium was officially closed to the public due to the 2015 Baltimore protests.

links.t: 2015 Chicago White Sox–Baltimore Orioles crowdless game

events.text: The Diocletianic Persecution of Christians officially ended in the eastern Roman Empire.
The Diocletianic Persecution of Christians in the Roman Empire ends.
Civil wars of the Tetrarchy: An outnumbered army led by Roman emperor Licinius defeated his rival Maximinus II's forces at the Battle of Tzirallum.
SN 1006, the brightest supernova in recorded history, first appeared in the constellation Lupus.
Roger de Flor, leader of the mercenary Catalan Company, is murdered, leading to widespread pillaging by the mercenaries in Thrace.
Enguerrand de Marigny is hanged at the instigation of Charles, Count of Valois.

main.desc: Royal court official under Philip IV of France

events.text: Spain gives Christopher Columbus his commission of exploration. He is named admiral of the ocean sea, viceroy and governor of any territory he discovers.
Edmund de la Pole, Yorkist pretender to the English throne, is executed on the orders of Henry VIII.

main.t: Edmund de la Pole, 3rd Duke of Suffolk

events.text: Juan de Oñate begins the conquest of Santa Fe de Nuevo México.

main.desc: 16/17th-century Spanish conquistador and colonial governor in New Spain

events.text: Henry IV of France issues the Edict of Nantes, allowing freedom of religion to the Huguenots.
Eighty Years' War: Dutch Republic forces recapture a strategically important fort from Spain after a nine-month siege.
George Washington (pictured) took the oath of office as the first president of the United States at Federal Hall in New York City.

main.desc: Founding Father, U.S. president from 1789 to 1797

links.t: Oath of office of the president of the United States

events.text: On the balcony of Federal Hall on Wall Street in New York City, George Washington takes the oath of office to become the first President of the United States.
The United States purchased France's claim to the Louisiana Territory for 80 million francs, or less than US$.03 per acre ($.07/ha).

main.desc: 1803 acquisition of region of Middle America land by the U.S. from France

events.text: Louisiana Purchase: The United States purchases the Louisiana Territory from France for $15 million, more than doubling the size of the young nation.
